architecture.approach: Rebuild the existing /admin console in place across five independently shippable milestones. Foundations land first (schema, audit literals, authorization helpers, formatters, CSV serializer, one analytics filter contract, shared panel states, navigation config); then the shell and command center; then the analytics workspace; then read-only operations (export, reports, health); then governance and feedback. Every new Convex function declares validators and authorizes server-side; the client guard stays defense in depth. No new runtime dependency, no second chart or table system, and no admin HTTP API are introduced.

fields.type: AuditAction (adds settings.updated, announcement.sent, feedback.updated, feedback.deleted, export.generated, maintenance.changed)

dataModel.flowDescription: Schema deploys first with new tables, indexes, and union literals, then helpers, audit, and rate limits, then query modules, then UI. The platform settings singleton is created lazily on first save; reads fall back to defaults when the document is absent. Analytics loads events through by_startDate (or by_category for a single category) and registrations through by_registeredAt or by_event_status, resolves one scope per handler, and echoes applied filters plus row counts. Exports reuse that scope. Broadcasts expand an audience into a recipient set, write delivery rows per recipient, and update counts. Feedback is created by signed-in users and mutated only by admins, with every mutation audited. Cron heartbeats and email outcomes feed the health panel. No backfill is required.

securityConsiderations.description: Every new Convex function resolves the Clerk identity and calls requireAdmin; feedback.submit requires a signed-in identity. requireSuperAdmin gates platform settings writes and every announcement mutation. Client hiding in AdminGuard and the sidebar is secondary only.

platform.updateSettings, announcements.resolveAudience, and announcements.send check super_admin inside the function after loading the caller record, so a direct client call cannot bypass the read-only page.

New @convex-dev/rate-limiter buckets: adminSearch (per admin, per minute), analytics, adminExport, broadcast, feedbackWrite, and feedback submit. Rejections return a retry hint that the UI renders verbatim.
Every Convex function declares convex/values arguments, including the shared analyticsFilterValidator; every new form validates with Zod before submission. No free-form object is accepted.
No dangerouslySetInnerHTML is introduced. Feedback messages, admin notes, and announcement bodies render as text nodes. CSV values are quoted and formula-neutralised per OWASP.
health.getOverview reports Boolean(process.env.X) only and never returns a value. Settings and health screens display presence labels. No .env file is created or modified.
proxy.ts, next.config.ts headers, and the hosting TLS/HSTS configuration are unchanged by this feature; no route disables transport enforcement.

Every administrative mutation calls logAdminAction inside the same mutation: settings.updated with a shallow before/after diff, announcement.sent with audience and counts, feedback.updated/feedback.deleted with changed fields, export.generated with module and row count, and maintenance.changed with the new state.

Feedback and announcement records are never purged automatically; only an explicit admin deletion removes them, and that deletion writes feedback.deleted with actor, target, and reason before the document is removed.

performanceConsiderations.strategy: Filtered windows are served by users.by_createdAt, registrations.by_registeredAt, registrations.by_event_status, events.by_startDate, events.by_category, and events.by_organizer; no filtered query collects a whole table. The three new indexes ship in the same schema deploy as the tables, and each filtered query's index usage is verified before the analytics flag is enabled. resolveAnalyticsScope runs once per handler and every aggregation derives from it. Results are bounded (palette 5 per group, queue 3 previews, exports 10,000 rows, lists 25) and panels fetch independently. Target: p95 <= 1.5 s analytics and <= 1 s dashboard at 50k events / 500k registrations; the fallback is a documented daily aggregate table, not heavier client work.
Each panel owns its loading state and renders a skeleton shaped like the final layout, so slow panels never block fast ones and layout shift is avoided.

risks.description: Read-on-demand analytics will not scale indefinitely and filtered queries could degrade at 10x current volume.
risks.mitigation: Index ranges, bounded windows, a single scope resolution per handler, a 10,000-row export cap, and a documented trigger point for a daily aggregate table.

risks.description: Broadcast email can damage sender reputation or spam users if enabled carelessly.
risks.mitigation: Broadcasts flag defaults off, super-admin only, masked preview with recipient count, typed confirmation, rate limit, batches of 50, and a per-recipient delivery log.

risks.description: Adding literals to the auditLogs unions is a schema change that can reject old documents when deployed out of order.
risks.mitigation: Deploy schema first with an exhaustive validator, deploy code second, and backfill no existing rows.

risks.description: CSV exports can leak personal data or execute spreadsheet formulas.
risks.mitigation: Admin-only, visible columns only, row cap, rate limit, audit entry per export, and OWASP-compliant quoting plus formula neutralisation.

risks.description: Maintenance mode can lock out legitimate operators.
risks.mitigation: Admins bypass the gate through the existing role query, enabling requires typed confirmation, the change is audited, and a banner shows while active.

risks.description: The public feedback form adds a new write surface.
risks.mitigation: Signed-in only, 10-2000 character message cap, event existence check, 10-minute duplicate suppression, rate limit, and no file uploads.

risks.description: Timezone-aware bucketing changes existing chart values relative to the current UTC behaviour.
risks.mitigation: Display the active timezone on every affected card, document the behaviour change in the plan, and bucket through Intl.DateTimeFormat with the platform timeZone.

risks.description: Palette search adds a query per keystroke and can overload the backend or the dialog.
risks.mitigation: Two-character minimum, 250 ms debounce, per-group caps of 5, an admin search rate limit, and inline retry instead of a blank panel.

risks.description: The scope spans thirteen stories and can be compressed into one risky release.
risks.mitigation: Five independently shippable milestones (M0-M4) plus a verification phase; each milestone can be reviewed and released behind its flag.
